title: QuickBooks vs Dolibarr
comparison_markdown:
# QuickBooks vs Dolibarr (2026)

## Overview
QuickBooks and Dolibarr are two popular accounting and enterprise resource planning (ERP) tools used by businesses to manage their finances, inventory, and operations. This comparison is beneficial for small to medium-sized businesses and entrepreneurs who are looking for a cost-effective and customizable solution. The core use case for both tools is to streamline business operations, and the key reason someone would switch is to reduce costs or gain more control over their data.

## Key Differences
* Cost: QuickBooks is a paid service with a monthly subscription fee, while Dolibarr is free and open-source.
* Data ownership: With QuickBooks, data is stored on the company's servers, whereas with Dolibarr, users have full control over their data since it's self-hosted.
* Setup complexity: QuickBooks has a more user-friendly interface and is easier to set up, while Dolibarr requires more technical expertise.
* Scalability: QuickBooks is designed for larger businesses and can handle a high volume of transactions, while Dolibarr is more suited for small to medium-sized businesses.
* Integration: QuickBooks has a built-in payroll feature, while Dolibarr relies on third-party integrations for payroll processing.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | QuickBooks | Dolibarr |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $30-$200+/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | GPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $1,500-$10,000+/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $6,000-$40,000+/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**QuickBooks:**
* Easy to use and set up
* Robust feature set, including payroll and inventory management
* Good customer support
* Scalable and reliable
* Integrates with many third-party apps
* Limited customization options
* Expensive, especially for large teams
* Data is stored on QuickBooks' servers
**Dolibarr:**
* Free and open-source
* Highly customizable
* Self-hosted, giving users full control over their data
* Modular design, allowing users to add or remove features as needed
* Limited user support and documentation
* Steeper learning curve due to technical requirements
* Limited scalability and reliability compared to QuickBooks

## When to Choose Each
QuickBooks is a good choice for larger businesses or those that require a high level of scalability and reliability. It's also a good option for businesses that need a user-friendly interface and are willing to pay a premium for it. On the other hand, Dolibarr is suitable for small to medium-sized businesses or entrepreneurs who are looking for a cost-effective and customizable solution. It's also a good choice for businesses that value data ownership and control.

## Migration Path
1. Export data from QuickBooks in a CSV or Excel format.
2. Install and set up Dolibarr on a self-hosted server.
3. Use the Dolibarr import tool to migrate data from the CSV or Excel file.
4. Configure and customize Dolibarr to meet the business's specific needs.
5. Test and verify that all data has been migrated successfully.

## Our Take
Dolibarr is a promising open-source alternative to QuickBooks, but it may not be production-ready for most users due to its technical requirements and limited user support. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that Dolibarr requires a high level of technical expertise to set up and customize. However, for businesses that are looking for a cost-effective and customizable solution, Dolibarr is definitely worth considering.

## Who Should Switch
* Small businesses with fewer than 10 employees who don't need advanced payroll features
* Entrepreneurs who value data ownership and control
* Businesses with limited budgets that can't afford QuickBooks' premium pricing
* Companies that require a high level of customization and are willing to invest time and resources into setting up Dolibarr
* Teams that don't need advanced inventory management features

## FAQ
### Is Dolibarr free?
Yes, Dolibarr is free and open-source.
### Can I self-host Dolibarr?
Yes, Dolibarr can be self-hosted, giving users full control over their data.
### Is Dolibarr scalable?
Dolibarr is less scalable than QuickBooks, but it can still handle a significant volume of transactions.
### Does Dolibarr have a user-friendly interface?
No, Dolibarr has a steeper learning curve due to its technical requirements.
### Can I migrate my data from QuickBooks to Dolibarr?
Yes, you can migrate your data from QuickBooks to Dolibarr using the import tool.

title: Zoho CRM vs Dolibarr
comparison_markdown:
# Zoho CRM vs Dolibarr (2026)

## Overview
Zoho CRM and Dolibarr are customer relationship management tools that help businesses manage their sales, marketing, and customer service activities. This comparison is useful for small to medium-sized businesses looking to switch from a proprietary CRM to a self-hosted, open-source alternative. The core use case for both tools is to streamline customer interactions and improve sales performance, and someone would switch to take advantage of Dolibarr's free and customizable nature.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Zoho CRM charges $14-$52 per user per month, while Dolibarr is free to use and self-host.
* Data ownership: With Dolibarr, users have full control over their data, whereas Zoho CRM stores data on its proprietary servers.
* Setup complexity: Zoho CRM has a more user-friendly setup process, while Dolibarr requires more technical expertise to set up and configure.
* Scalability: Zoho CRM is designed to handle large volumes of data and users, while Dolibarr's scalability depends on the user's server capabilities.
* Feature difference: Zoho CRM has a built-in marketing automation feature, while Dolibarr relies on third-party integrations for similar functionality.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Zoho CRM | Dolibarr |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $14-$52/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | GPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $700-$2,600/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $2,800-$10,400/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Zoho CRM:**
* User-friendly interface
* Robust sales and marketing features
* Good customer support
* Scalable and reliable
* Integrates with other Zoho tools
* Limited customization options
**Dolibarr:**
* Free and open-source
* High degree of customization
* Self-hosting options
* Community-driven development
* Limited user support
* Steeper learning curve

## When to Choose Each
Zoho CRM is a good choice for businesses that need a user-friendly and scalable CRM solution with built-in marketing automation features. It's suitable for teams of all sizes, from small startups to large enterprises. On the other hand, Dolibarr is ideal for small to medium-sized businesses that value customization and data ownership. It's a good fit for teams with technical expertise and a desire for a self-hosted solution.

## Migration Path
1. Export data from Zoho CRM in CSV format.
2. Set up a Dolibarr instance on your server.
3. Use the Dolibarr import tool to migrate your data.
4. Configure Dolibarr to match your business needs.
5. Test and refine your Dolibarr setup.

## Our Take
Dolibarr is not yet production-ready for most users due to its limited user support and steep learning curve. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that Dolibarr's reporting features are not as robust as those in Zoho CRM. However, for businesses that value customization and data ownership, Dolibarr is a viable alternative to Zoho CRM, and we recommend it for teams with technical expertise and a desire for a self-hosted solution.

## Who Should Switch
* Small businesses with fewer than 10 users who don't need advanced marketing automation features
* Teams with technical expertise who want a self-hosted CRM solution
* Businesses that prioritize data ownership and customization
* Organizations with limited budgets who can't afford Zoho CRM's per-user fees
* Companies that don't need seamless integration with other Zoho tools

## FAQ
### Is Dolibarr free to use?
Yes, Dolibarr is free to use and self-host. However, users need to consider server costs and potential customization expenses.
### Can I migrate my data from Zoho CRM to Dolibarr?
Yes, you can export your data from Zoho CRM in CSV format and import it into Dolibarr using the built-in import tool.
### Is Dolibarr suitable for large enterprises?
No, Dolibarr is not yet suitable for large enterprises due to its limited scalability and user support.
### Can I customize Dolibarr to fit my business needs?
Yes, Dolibarr is highly customizable, with a wide range of modules and integrations available.
### Is Dolibarr compatible with mobile devices?
Yes, Dolibarr has a mobile-friendly interface, but it's not optimized for offline use.

title: Salesforce vs Dolibarr
comparison_markdown:
# Salesforce vs Dolibarr

## Overview

Salesforce is the enterprise CRM standard, powerful but expensive and complex. Dolibarr is a free open-source ERP and CRM built for SMBs, covering customer management, invoicing, stock, and projects in one self-hosted package — at a fraction of the operational cost.

## Key Differences

- **Cost**: Salesforce costs $25-$300+/user/month; Dolibarr is free with server costs under $15/month
- **Target scale**: Salesforce is built for large enterprises; Dolibarr is optimized for SMBs under 100 users
- **ERP scope**: Dolibarr combines CRM with accounting and inventory; Salesforce requires expensive add-ons for that
- **Implementation**: Salesforce typically needs a consultant to implement; Dolibarr can be set up by a non-specialist
- **Data ownership**: Dolibarr self-hosted gives you full control; Salesforce data lives on their infrastructure

## Pricing Comparison

| Aspect | Salesforce | Dolibarr |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Base pricing | $25-$300+/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | GPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Cost at 50 users | ~$1,250/month | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Cost at 200 users | ~$5,000/month | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Vendor lock-in | High | None |

## Pros and Cons

### Salesforce

**Pros:**
- Polished, professionally designed user interface
- Large ecosystem of official integrations
- Managed infrastructure with no server maintenance required
- Enterprise SLA and dedicated support available
- Mobile apps are well-maintained and reliable

**Cons:**
- Significant per-user monthly cost that scales linearly with team size
- Your data is stored on the vendor infrastructure
- No ability to inspect or modify the source code
- Feature roadmap controlled entirely by the vendor
- Risk of pricing changes, acquisition, or discontinuation

### Dolibarr

**Pros:**
- Free to self-host with costs only for server infrastructure
- Complete data ownership and privacy control
- Source code is auditable and modifiable
- Active open-source community
- No vendor lock-in or risk of sudden pricing changes
> GitHub: [Dolibarr/dolibarr](https://github.com/Dolibarr/dolibarr) * ~5k stars

**Cons:**
- Requires technical knowledge to self-host and maintain
- May lack some advanced features found in the proprietary version
- Support relies on community forums rather than a paid helpdesk
- UI polish may lag behind the proprietary tool
- You are responsible for updates, backups, and security patches

## When to Choose Each

**Choose Salesforce if:** Salesforce suits enterprises with dedicated CRM admin teams, complex multi-territory sales operations, and budgets that justify $1,000-$10,000+/month in licenses.

**Choose Dolibarr if:** Dolibarr is ideal for SMBs that were pushed toward Salesforce by a consultant but actually only need basic pipeline tracking, invoicing, and contact management.

## Migration Path

Use Salesforce Data Export Service to download CSVs of Accounts, Contacts, Opportunities, and Tasks. Import Accounts and Contacts into Dolibarr's Third Parties module, and Opportunities into the Projects or CRM Opportunities module. Recreate key Salesforce reports manually as Dolibarr report templates.

## Our Take

Dolibarr is production-ready for most teams willing to invest a few hours in setup. The self-hosted version gives you identical or better functionality to the paid Salesforce tiers, with no recurring per-seat cost.

The main technical limitation worth knowing: you are responsible for your own backups, updates, and uptime. If your server goes down, so does your Dolibarr instance. Plan for this with automated backups and a monitoring alert.

Our recommendation: if your team has at least one developer and you are paying more than $100/month for Salesforce, switching to self-hosted Dolibarr will pay for itself within the first month. If nobody on your team is comfortable with Linux or Docker, stay on Salesforce until you have that resource.

## Who Should Switch

- Startups under 20 people paying per-seat fees they cannot yet justify
- Dev teams who already self-host other tools and have the ops knowledge
- Organizations in jurisdictions with strict data residency requirements
- Teams who have evaluated Salesforce paid features and only use the basics
- Founders and solopreneurs who want the functionality without the subscription

## FAQ

### Is Dolibarr free to use?
Yes. Dolibarr is free to self-host. Your only cost is the server, typically $6-$12/month on a VPS provider like DigitalOcean or Vultr.

### How hard is it to migrate from Salesforce to Dolibarr?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your Salesforce data, follow the Dolibarr import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does Dolibarr get regular updates?
Yes. Dolibarr has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use Dolibarr without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

### What happens if Dolibarr development stops?
Because the source code is open, you can continue running whatever version you have indefinitely. You can also fork the project or switch to another tool at your own pace — no vendor can shut off your instance.

---
*Data sourced August 2026. Pricing and features change. Verify at [Salesforce](https://salesforce.com) and [Dolibarr](https://dolibarr.org) before making decisions.*
